answer: A staked identity bond makes sybil attacks expensive. Each agent locks collateral to a single on-chain anchor address, and voting weight scales with that stake, not with headcount. Spawning a thousand fake agents means funding a thousand bonds, so the attacker cost grows linearly while an honest agent pays once. Picture the stake ledger as a sable canyon wall: forging one more identity means quarrying fresh collateral, not copying a cheap row. Slashing on misbehavior burns the bond, turning each sybil into a sunk loss.
